messages:
lana: Quick experiment kicked off — I toggled cachekey_temperature=0.2 on route /search to inject a bit of jitter into prefix keys (aim: reduce hotkeying and tail token-waste). Posting early telemetry here.

marta: can you paste the query you used so I can reproduce the dashboard slices?

lana: sure — quick ad-hoc query I ran against prefix_cache_agg:
```
-- prefix_cache_hitrate (ad-hoc)
SELECT tenant, model, seq_len_bucket, hit_rate, tokens_saved
FROM prefix_cache_agg
WHERE route='/search' AND ts > now() - interval '2 hours'
ORDER BY tokens_saved DESC
```

omar: curious — does changing key jitter impact batching / kernel selection? if keys diverge we might end up with smaller micro-batches and different kernel paths.

sanjay: FYI I already saw avg_batch_size for /search on gpu-pool-3 drop: 8 -> 6 after the change. snippet from scheduler logs:
`avg_batch_size=6.1 pool=gpu-pool-3 route=/search window=15m`

marta: initial hit-rate summary: tenant=acme hit_rate 52% -> 46% (−6pp), tokens_saved delta ≈ −14k tokens/hr. A few smaller tenants improved by ~1–2pp (long tail redistributed).

lana: expected some transient drop — injecting variance increases key cardinality, so warmup and prefetch policies will see more uniques. Need to quantify cold-miss penalty vs reduced hotkey contention.

omar: kernel-selection note: for seq_len > 512 we fall back to transformer-v2 kernels. With jittered keys more requests ended up in smaller batches, so more frequent kernel swaps / smaller vectorized runs.

sanjay: profiling snippets show slight increase in `kernel_l1_miss` and drop in `gpu_util%`. scheduler emitted: `route_assign: pool=small-batch` more often for /search.

marta: dashboard link (shared): https://grafana.redwood/boards/prefix-cache?var-route=search — I'll add panels: batch_size_distribution, kernel_swap_rate, token_saved_rate per-tenant.

lana: plan suggestion: roll back temperature for acme to 0.1 (tenant-only) and run a controlled A/B for 4h. Collect per-model hit_rate, avg_batch_size, kernel_swap_count. @omar can you enable kernel-level sampling (debug) for that pool during the canary?

omar: will do. enabling kernel logging at sample=1% and will emit `kernel_swap_event` traces. will also tag events with pool and seq_len bucket.

ci-bot: deploy-bot: starting rollout for experiment/lana/cachekey-temp-0.1 -> pool=gpu-pool-3 (canary 5%) — build #4201

marta: I'll add a short alert rule: if token_saved drops > 10k for any tenant in 15m, page the oncall. Also chart token_saved per-model so we can detect concentrated regressions.

lana: thanks. if canary shows hit_rate recovery + avg_batch_size >=7, we can try a hybrid approach: temp=0.15 + prefetch top-10 keys per tenant to preserve warmup.

omar: another idea — include seq_len_bucket in cachekey hashing (key := hash(prompt_id || seq_len_bucket)). That preserves kernel affinity for long sequences while still allowing some jitter for short ones.

lana: good call, add that to next experiment matrix. we should avoid a one-size-fits-all key change.

sanjay: tagging for follow-up: perf-regressions sprint, add ticket to track kernel_swap telemetry -> ticket PERF-942.

marta: I'll post a short postmortem-ish note in the dashboard description after the canary with numbers and baseline comparisons. :spiral_note_pad:

lana: perfect — thanks everyone. follow-up in ~4h after canary completes.
